turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sitting down. I have a client call at 4:40, so I have about twenty minutes. Owen found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of your class. Start there.
Hale, I'm not here for pleasantries. You said "thanks for coming in," so tell me what the zero is based on.
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.
Don't manage me. He found out about the zero on his phone, Hale, in your class. Was he asked about the essay before that happened, yes or no?
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.
"Misunderstanding" is a word for a conversation that hasn't happened yet. Did anyone speak to Owen before the mark went into the gradebook?
So can we agree he's a good student?
I'm not agreeing to anything about Owen until I know what the zero is based on. You haven't answered my question. Did anyone speak to him before the mark was entered?
